assessment: This work presents a different US perspective for cancer screenings among the least screened women, those 50-64 years old. Using the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System and the two cancer screenings (cervical and colorectal) done by her primary care physician, the findings of this work show that women-centric screening is lower than single cancer screenings. There is a large gap in health systems processes to meet the cancer screening needs of each woman.
